newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - Aug 5.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THACKERAY'S THREAT TO PASWAN ROCKS PARLIAMENT

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-Shiv Sena party combine and other political parties fought a war of words in parliament over a reported threat by Bal Thackeray to bar Railway Minister Ram Vilas Paswan from entering Maharashtra state. The BJP-Shiv Sena members said the threat by the Shiv Sena chief reflected the people's anger as their longstanding demand for a Konkan railway train was not met. They said Thackeray's statement was only a form of protest and was unlikely to be translated into action. But opponents took strong exception to such threats being directed at a union minister.
SEBI ASKS INDUSTRIAL BANK TO DECLARE FUTURE PLANS

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) concluded that the disclosures of ICICI Bank's letter of offer for its public issue were inadequate. It directed Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India (ICICI) to declare its future plans. The SEBI directive followed a recent statement by ICICI officials that it was planning to become a bank in the next 18 months. The statement prompted speculation that ICICI Bank might eventually merge with ICICI.
GOVERNMENT POSTPONES IMPLEMENTATION OF NEW PAY SCALE

The government has decided to withhold the implementation of revised pay scales involving a package of 135 billion rupees to its 5,200,000 employees. The employees said the revised pay scales were inadequate and had threatened to strike work. The cabinet secretary said the government went way beyond the fifth pay commission recommendations and felt the new pay package was quite generous.

The National Stock Exchange decided to do away with the five-year lock-in period on members' deposits to provide an exit route to members waiting to opt out of the exchange's membership. The bourse, however, decided to continue with the option of membership withdrawal without being subject to a five-year lock-in period for deposits.
